maria_support: Hey @customer_acme — thanks for the signal. Can you grab the request ID (or debug token) from the failing call so we can pull the server-side trace? Minimal things we need: 1) the request-id or debug token, 2) a curl that reproduces (or HAR), 3) approximate client time + region.
customer_acme: Hey — we saw a 401 and a bunch of timeouts around 11:03am PT. We don't see an obvious request-id in our app logs. Is that the X-Request-ID header? Where should we look in the Redwood Console?
liz_dev: For Console: go to Console -> Requests (left nav) -> filter by time -> open the row for the request -> top section shows "request_id" and "trace_token". Copy the request_id (looks like a short hex). If you don't see it, try the Network tab in your browser devtools and inspect the response headers — we send `x-request-id` and `x-debug-token` in responses.
maria_support: If you're using our JS/TS SDK, look for `request_id` in the SDK debug logs. Example grep from your server (if logs are JSON):
```bash
# if SDK logs JSON to stdout/stderr
grep request_id /var/log/my-app.log | tail -n 20
# pretty-print one line
echo '{...json...}' | jq '.request_id, .status, .error'
```
customer_acme: we run the node sdk in a lambda. Our cloudwatch logs are noisy. Any quick grep that looks for both the header and body?
andrews: Try this CloudWatch Insights query (replace /aws/lambda/your-fn):
fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /request_id|x-request-id|X-Request-ID/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 50
Also the SDK prints a short line: `handled request id=abcd1234 latency=345ms` by default when DEBUG=redwood.
liz_dev: If you can run a local curl repro, that helps a lot. Example to force a similar auth flow (redact API key):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACT-API-KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Request-ID: repro-abc-123" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
The `-v` output will show response headers including `x-request-id` and `x-debug-token`. Paste the `x-debug-token` if present — it helps us fetch a fully indexed debug bundle.
customer_acme: ok copying steps. We can run curl and paste the headers. For the lambda logs we found a line: `handled request id=6f9a3b2b latency=1200ms status=401`. Does that look right?
maria_support: Perfect — that's the request id we need. Two quick asks: 1) paste the full `handled request id=6f9a3b2b` line (or the CloudWatch event), 2) run the curl with `X-Request-ID` set to the same id so we can correlate on our side. Example: `-H "X-Request-ID: 6f9a3b2b"`
customer_acme: pasted the log line above and ran the curl. Here's the response headers from `-v`:
```
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-request-id: 6f9a3b2b
< x-debug-token: dbg_7c8f5a
< content-type: application/json
```
liz_dev: Nice — that `x-debug-token: dbg_7c8f5a` is ideal. Please don't paste your API key. We'll fetch the debug bundle `dbg_7c8f5a` (server-side) and inspect auth checks + rate-limit traces.
maria_support: I've opened an internal ticket and pinned the request id + debug token. Tagging @andrews for deeper auth traces and @liz_dev for repro follow-up. :mag:
andrews: On it. If the debug bundle shows an upstream 401, we'll check KMS rotation events and recent policy updates. Could you also confirm the account billing status in Console -> Billing -> Payment methods? Sometimes 401s come from account-level blocks.
customer_acme: billing looks fine, no recent changes. Thanks — appreciate the quick follow-up.
deploy-bot: deploy started: inference-runtime v3.12.4 by liz_dev at 2026-05-17T17:40:10Z :rocket:
maria_support: Thanks team — we'll update once we pull the debug bundle. If you want us to redact logs on our side, say so and we can highlight only the `request_id` and `x-debug-token` sections. :white_check_mark:
